summary: Nike reported a quarter with falling revenue but better gross margin, guided to a high-single-digit revenue decline for the year, and announced the Pace restructuring with large charges and long-dated savings. The stock has already fallen sharply, so the negatives look partly priced in while the cost program offers some offset. The net effect against the S&P 500 is unclear.

flags.why: The earnings release pairs a full-year outlook for a high-single-digit revenue decline with an adjusted profit range and a better gross margin.
flags.quote: Revenues are expected to decline high-single digits in fiscal 2027

flags.why: The Pace program is a large multi-year restructuring with sizeable charges up front and savings spread over several years.
flags.quote: The Company expects the program to deliver approximately $2.5 billion in cumulative savings through fiscal 2031.

evidence_for.claim: Pace is expected to deliver about $2.5 billion in cumulative savings.
evidence_for.quote: The Company expects the program to deliver approximately $2.5 billion in cumulative savings through fiscal 2031

evidence_for.claim: Gross margin expanded 60 basis points to 42.8 percent, helped by lower logistics costs.
evidence_for.quote: Gross margin expanded 60 basis points to 42.8 percent, primarily due to lower warehousing and logistics costs.

evidence_against.claim: Management expects revenue to decline by a high-single-digit percentage for the full year.
evidence_against.quote: Revenues are expected to decline high-single digits in fiscal 2027

evidence_against.claim: First quarter revenues fell 4 percent on a reported basis.
evidence_against.quote: First quarter revenues were $11.2 billion, down 4 percent on a reported basis

would_change_call: Evidence that revenue is stabilizing faster than the decline guided, or a further guidance cut, would move the call toward Bullish or Bearish.

problems: evidence_against[1].claim: numbers ['2027'] not in the cited quote or price inputs
